title: Rigveda 10.116: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.116: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.116 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 103r-104r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.116.1 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 103r
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>pibā̱ soma̍m maha̱ta i̍ndri̱yāya̱ pibā̍ vṛ̱trāya̱ hanta̍ve śaviṣṭha | piba̍ rā̱ye śava̍se hū̱yamā̍na̱ḥ piba̱ madhva̍s tṛ̱pad i̱ndrā vṛ̍ṣasva ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vr̥itra. Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 103r (OPenn image 102, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.115.7 ‹-ṣṭave sahasaḥ sūnaro nṛbhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 103v, begins in RV 10.116.2 ‹-kṣumataḥ prasthitasyendra somasya varam›. Verse 10.116.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.116.2-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 103v
translation.original_text:
2a̱sya pi̍ba kṣu̱mata̱ḥ prasthi̍ta̱syendra̱ soma̍sya̱ vara̱m ā su̱tasya̍ | sva̱sti̱dā mana̍sā mādayasvārvācī̱no re̱vate̱ saubha̍gāya ||
3ma̱mattu̍ tvā di̱vyaḥ soma̍ indra ma̱mattu̱ yaḥ sū̱yate̱ pārthi̍veṣu | ma̱mattu̱ yena̱ vari̍vaś ca̱kartha̍ ma̱mattu̱ yena̍ niri̱ṇāsi̱ śatrū̍n ||
4ā dvi̱barhā̍ ami̱no yā̱tv indro̱ vṛṣā̱ hari̍bhyā̱m pari̍ṣikta̱m andha̍ḥ | gavy ā su̱tasya̱ prabhṛ̍tasya̱ madhva̍ḥ sa̱trā khedā̍m aruśa̱hā vṛ̍ṣasva ||
5ni ti̱gmāni̍ bhrā̱śaya̱n bhrāśyā̱ny ava̍ sthi̱rā ta̍nuhi yātu̱jūnā̍m | u̱grāya̍ te̱ saho̱ bala̍ṁ dadāmi pra̱tītyā̱ śatrū̍n viga̱deṣu̍ vṛśca ||
translation.text:
2Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma. Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper.
3Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee. Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen.
4Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers. With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer.
5Dash down, outffaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons. I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 103v (OPenn image 103, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.116.2 ‹-kṣumataḥ prasthitasyendra somasya varam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 104r, begins in RV 10.116.6 ‹ojaḥ sthireva dhanvano 'bhimātīḥ›. Verses 10.116.2-5 end on this page; 10.116.2 begins on fol. 103r.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.116.6-9 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 104r
translation.original_text:
6vy a1̱̍rya i̍ndra tanuhi̱ śravā̱ṁsy oja̍ḥ sthi̱reva̱ dhanva̍no̱ 'bhimā̍tīḥ | a̱sma̱drya̍g vāvṛdhā̱naḥ saho̍bhi̱r ani̍bhṛṣṭas ta̱nva̍ṁ vāvṛdhasva ||
7i̱daṁ ha̱vir ma̍ghava̱n tubhya̍ṁ rā̱tam prati̍ samrā̱ḻ ahṛ̍ṇāno gṛbhāya | tubhya̍ṁ su̱to ma̍ghava̱n tubhya̍m pa̱kvo̱3̱̍ 'ddhī̍ndra̱ piba̍ ca̱ prasthi̍tasya ||
8a̱ddhīd i̍ndra̱ prasthi̍te̱mā ha̱vīṁṣi̱ cano̍ dadhiṣva paca̱tota soma̍m | praya̍svanta̱ḥ prati̍ haryāmasi tvā sa̱tyāḥ sa̍ntu̱ yaja̍mānasya̱ kāmā̍ḥ ||
9prendrā̱gnibhyā̍ṁ suvaca̱syām i̍yarmi̱ sindhā̍v iva̱ prera̍ya̱ṁ nāva̍m a̱rkaiḥ | ayā̍ iva̱ pari̍ caranti de̱vā ye a̱smabhya̍ṁ dhana̱dā u̱dbhida̍ś ca ||
translation.text:
6Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman. Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body.
7To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger. Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee.
8Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma. With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes.
9I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters. Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 104r (OPenn image 103, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.116.6 ‹ojaḥ sthireva dhanvano 'bhimātīḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 104v, begins in RV 10.117.1 ‹-utāśitam upa gacchanti mṛtyavaḥ›. Verses 10.116.6-9 end on this page; 10.116.6 begins on fol. 103v.
